name: Route quote requests from multiple IMAP mailboxes to HubSpot with duplicate check

parameters.content:
## Route quote requests to HubSpot

Watches two shared mailboxes (for example the sales and the info inbox). Every new email is normalized, classified by product group and checked for duplicates within the run.

Clear requests create or update a HubSpot contact and notify the responsible sales owner. Incomplete, ambiguous or duplicate requests go to a manual review inbox instead of the CRM.

Generic example, no client data. Replace every YOUR_* placeholder before use.

### 1. Intake (two IMAP triggers)
Each mailbox is its own Email Trigger (IMAP). Whichever mailbox fires starts the run and walks the same path. Point the mailbox parameter of each node at one shared folder.

### 2. Routing config (Set node)
Owner per product group, fallback owner, review inbox and sender address live here. Edit this node, not the Code node. Mailbox folders are set in the two IMAP nodes; the admin alert and its sender address live in the Alert Admin node itself (see error path note).

### 3. Classification + duplicate check (Code node)
Extracts sender, subject and body preview, derives the product group from keywords and flags: missing sender/subject, unknown product group, no owner mapped, or sender + subject already seen in this run (the IMAP "simple" format has no top-level Message-ID or attachment names, so the owner email's Attachments line stays empty). The config values are copied into each output item so later nodes never fall back to placeholders.

### 4. CRM + owner notification
Upserts one HubSpot contact keyed by the sender email (create or update — no duplicate contacts). Because HubSpot replaces the item data, the email node reads all values from the Prepare Request Data node, not from $json. HubSpot stands for any CRM with an n8n node; swap the node to match yours.

### 5. Manual review
Everything the classifier is not sure about lands here with a reason, instead of touching the CRM. The review inbox is the single place a human has to watch.

### Error path
All nodes with external dependencies (IMAP, HubSpot, SMTP) use "On Error: Continue (using error output)" — except Alert Admin on Error, which continues on its regular output. Their error outputs meet in Log Error, which mails the admin. The admin address is set directly in the Alert Admin node, not in Routing Config. Trigger failures (for example the IMAP connection) never reach an error output: n8n runs the workflow's Error Workflow instead, so register a separate workflow with an Error Trigger under Settings → Error workflow.
